# Kinetiq — full reference

> A React component library where every animation shares five calibrated springs. Copy the source. Own the code. Ship interfaces that feel machined.

Machine catalog: https://kinetiqui.vercel.app/registry-meta.json · MCP server: https://kinetiqui.vercel.app/mcp

## Operating rules (AGENTS.md)

# Kinetiq — Agent Rules

Operating rules for coding agents working with Kinetiq components. Follow
these and anything you compose stays on the system's motion vocabulary.

## The motion language: five calibrated springs

Every animation uses exactly one of five springs from `lib/motion.ts`. Never
hand-write stiffness/damping numbers — reach for a named spring.

| Spring | stiffness / damping / mass | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `flick` | 1100 / 55 / 0.7 | Press states, tick draws, focus. **Confirms.** |
| `snap` | 640 / 42 / 1.0 | Toggles, tab indicators, menus. One crisp overshoot. **Switches.** |
| `glide` | 300 / 34 / 1.0 | Layout shifts, reorders, morphs. **Moves.** |
| `drift` | 120 / 24 / 1.2 | Large surfaces, ambient motion, parallax settle. **Breathes.** |
| `recoil` | 520 / 24 / 1.0 | Toasts, stamps, landings. Two visible bounces. **Celebrates.** |

Say the verb the interaction performs — confirm, switch, move, breathe,
celebrate — and you have the spring.

## Tweens, not springs, for surface properties

Springs drive spatial change (position, scale, rotation). Opacity, color,
blur, and clip use the tween scale from `lib/motion.ts`:

- Durations: `blink 0.08` · `fast 0.15` · `base 0.24` · `slow 0.40` · `page 0.70`
- Easings: `enter [0.22,1,0.36,1]` · `exit [0.5,0,0.75,0]` · `move [0.65,0,0.35,1]` · `linear`
- Enter offsets: `nudge 4` · `step 8` · `shift 16` (px). Scale-ins start at 0.96, never 0.

## Orchestration

- **600ms budget.** A choreographed sequence never exceeds 600ms total. Use
  `cascade(count)` for the stagger interval — it tightens automatically as the
  count grows.
- **Exits are tweens at 0.6x the enter duration** with the `exit` easing, via
  `exitFor()`. Never spring an exit — it reads as indecision.
- One spatial axis per element; stagger from the element the user touched.

## Reduced motion is a first-class state

Read `useMotionSafe()` — never call `matchMedia` directly. When it returns
false, degrade, do not disable:

- Transform enters → opacity fade at `fast`.
- Discrete springs → instant position + a color tween.
- Direct manipulation (drag, sliders) → keep 1:1 tracking; drop inertia and settle.
- Autoplay loops → static (marquees become a wrapped grid).
- Scroll-linked → final state, opacity only. Number rolls → instant value + highlight.

## Tokens

Use shadcn semantic tokens only: `bg-background/card/popover/primary/muted/accent/destructive`,
`text-*-foreground`, `border-border/input`, `ring`. For live-data accents
(readouts, traces, LIVE badges) use `var(--signal, var(--primary))`. Radii:
`rounded-1` (2px) · `rounded-2` (6px) · `rounded-3` (10px) · `rounded-4` (16px).

## Accessibility

Every interactive component ships real WAI-ARIA roles, complete keyboard
support, and visible focus rings (`:focus-visible`, never removed). Silent
state changes announce through an sr-only live region.

## Installing

Components are distributed as source through a shadcn-compatible registry.

```sh
# One-time: register the namespace
npx shadcn@latest registry add @kinetiq=https://kinetiqui.vercel.app/r/{name}.json
# Then add by name
npx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/pressure-button
# Or zero-config by URL
npx shadcn@latest add https://kinetiqui.vercel.app/r/pressure-button.json
```

Installed components import shared helpers (`lib/motion`, `lib/utils`, the
`use-motion-safe` hook) via your project's aliases — the CLI rewrites them on
install. Don't edit those shared files per-component; they're the shared
vocabulary.

## Motion system

Five calibrated springs — every animation uses one of them:

- `springs.flick` — stiffness 1100, damping 55, mass 0.7 (ζ 0.99, settles ~120ms). Press states, tick draws, focus. Confirms.
- `springs.snap` — stiffness 640, damping 42, mass 1 (ζ 0.83, settles ~300ms). Toggles, tab indicators, menus — one crisp overshoot. Switches.
- `springs.glide` — stiffness 300, damping 34, mass 1 (ζ 0.98, settles ~450ms). Layout shifts, reorders, morphs. Moves.
- `springs.drift` — stiffness 120, damping 24, mass 1.2 (ζ 1, settles ~800ms). Large surfaces, ambient drift, parallax settle. Breathes.
- `springs.recoil` — stiffness 520, damping 24, mass 1 (ζ 0.53, settles ~700ms). Toasts, stamps, landings — two visible bounces. Celebrates.

Cascade: Stagger interval = clamp(0.6 / (count - 1), 0.02, 0.06)s so the whole choreography stays under a 600ms budget; dense lists tighten automatically.
Exits: Exits are always tweens at 0.6x the enter duration with the exit easing — springs on exit read as indecision.
Reduced motion: prefers-reduced-motion is a first-class state. Transform enters become opacity fades; discrete springs snap to position with a color tween; direct manipulation keeps 1:1 tracking but drops inertia; autoplay loops go static; scroll-linked renders its final frame; number rolls swap instantly. Every component reads useMotionSafe(), never matchMedia directly.

## Catalog

### Pressure Button (KQ-001) — `pressure-button`
A button that pushes back.

A button that pushes back — press squash on flick, spring rebound on snap, and a hold-to-confirm gauge ring for destructive actions.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/pressure-button`

Props:
- `variant`: "solid" | "outline" | "ghost" | "danger" (default "solid") — Visual style. Danger pairs naturally with holdToConfirm.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — Control height and typography scale.
- `holdToConfirm`: number — Milliseconds the button must be held before confirming. Adds a gauge ring; Escape or early release cancels.
- `onConfirm`: () => void — Fires when a hold completes. Hold buttons never fire onClick.

Notes:
- Space and Enter drive the same physics as the pointer — hold either to confirm.
- Under reduced motion the squash is replaced by a shade change; the gauge ring still fills because progress is feedback, not flourish.

### Trace Input (KQ-002) — `trace-input`
Focus draws its own boundary.

A plain text field with the focus drawn rather than switched on. A stroke traces the field's perimeter as it takes focus and the label warms to the ring colour; errors nudge the box and annotate themselves with a dimension line. The label sits above the box, so the affixes and the text share one centred line inside it.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/trace-input`

Props:
- `label`: string — Field label, rendered above the box. Pass labelHidden to keep it for assistive tech only.
- `description / error`: string — Helper and error lines below the field, chained into aria-describedby. Errors nudge the field and set aria-invalid.
- `prefix / suffix`: ReactNode — Leading and trailing slots inside the field.
- `…input props`: Omit<InputProps, "prefix"> — Standard input passthrough; controlled and uncontrolled both work.

Notes:
- The perimeter trace doubles as the focus indicator — it is never removed, only accelerated.
- The label is above the box, so pass a placeholder for hint text inside it; nothing is reserved and every child stays centred.
- Under reduced motion the stroke appears instantly and the error nudge is skipped; the message still announces via aria-invalid.

### Breaker Switch (KQ-003) — `breaker-switch`
A toggle with mechanical conviction.

A toggle with mechanical conviction — the thumb stretches in anticipation while held, throws on snap, and squashes against the track end as the rail recoils.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/breaker-switch`

Props:
- `checked / defaultChecked / onCheckedChange`: boolean / boolean / (checked) => void — Controlled or uncontrolled state.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — Fixed geometry — travel is derived, nothing is measured.
- `onLabel / offLabel`: string — Tiny uppercase text inside the track ends.
- `label`: ReactNode — Adjacent clickable label, associated automatically.
- `name / value`: string — Renders a hidden input that submits while checked.

Notes:
- A native button with role="switch" — Space and Enter throw it, and Space arms the anticipation stretch.
- Under reduced motion the thumb repositions instantly; only the color crossfade remains.

### Checkbox (KQ-004) — `checkbox`
The tick is drawn, not shown.

The tick is drawn, not shown — a pathLength stroke on flick, an indeterminate dash that slides in, and group select-alls that cascade down the list.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/checkbox`

Props:
- `checked / defaultChecked`: boolean — Controlled or uncontrolled checked state.
- `indeterminate`: boolean (default false) — Mixed state — dash visual plus native el.indeterminate.
- `onCheckedChange`: (checked: boolean) => void — Fires with the next checked state.
- `label / description`: ReactNode — Visible label (required) and muted secondary line.
- `CheckboxGroup`: items, value, onValueChange, selectAll, legend… — Fieldset-based group with select-all parent (checked / unchecked / indeterminate) and cascading tick draws.

Notes:
- Native hidden inputs do the accessibility work; the drawn box is decorative.
- Under reduced motion ticks appear instantly and select-all cascades lose their stagger.

### Caliper Slider (KQ-005) — `caliper-slider`
Reads like a vernier, moves like grease.

Reads like a vernier, moves like grease — 1:1 drag with a snap settle, ticks that lean toward the jaw, and a live measured-span dimension line in range mode.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/caliper-slider`

Props:
- `min / max / step`: number (default 0 / 100 / 1) — Bounds and snap grid (float-precision cleaned).
- `value / defaultValue / onValueChange`: number | [number, number] — Single or range; live stepped values during drag, deduped.
- `range`: boolean (default false) — Two facing caliper jaws with a live span dimension line.
- `marks`: number[] | boolean (default true) — Every step when ≤ 40 steps, else quarters; or pinned positions.
- `format / readout`: (v) => string / "float" | "end" | "none" — Value formatting and where the mono readout renders.

Notes:
- Full APG slider keyboard set per thumb; range thumbs cross-clamp their ARIA bounds.
- Under reduced motion tracking stays 1:1 — only the tick lean and the settle spring are removed.

### Gantry Tabs (KQ-006) — `gantry-tabs`
The indicator rides a rail.

The indicator rides a rail — its leading edge glides ahead while the trailing edge lags a beat, stretching toward the destination before contracting to fit.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/gantry-tabs`

Props:
- `value / defaultValue / onValueChange`: string / string / (value) => void — Controlled or uncontrolled active tab.
- `variant`: "underline" | "segmented" | "enclosed" (default "underline") — Indicator style.
- `orientation`: "horizontal" | "vertical" (default "horizontal") — Layout and arrow-key axis.
- `activationMode`: "automatic" | "manual" (default "automatic") — Activate on focus, or on Enter/Space.
- `keepMounted`: boolean (default false) — Keep inactive panels mounted but hidden.

Notes:
- Full APG tabs keyboard support with wrapping arrows; disabled triggers are skipped.
- Under reduced motion the indicator teleports and panels crossfade without the lift.

### Drawer Accordion (KQ-007) — `drawer-accordion`
Opens like a specimen cabinet.

Opens like a specimen cabinet — height glides while the inner content lags a beat behind, like paper settling in a pulled drawer.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/drawer-accordion`

Props:
- `type`: "single" | "multiple" (default "single") — Open one drawer at a time, or many.
- `value / defaultValue`: string | string[] — Controlled or uncontrolled open value(s).
- `onValueChange`: (value) => void — Fires with the next open value(s).
- `collapsible`: boolean (default true) — Single mode: allow closing the open item.
- `Item.value / Item.disabled`: string / boolean — Unique drawer id; disabled items are skipped in arrow navigation.
- `Trigger.icon`: ReactNode — Leading icon slot before the header label.

Notes:
- Full APG accordion keyboard support: Arrow keys move between headers, Home and End jump.
- Under reduced motion drawers open instantly and content crossfades — no lag, no sibling nudge.

### Callout (KQ-008) — `callout`
A label with a leader line.

A tooltip with a leader line — the label pops from the anchor while a schematic elbow line draws itself to the card.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/callout`

Props:
- `content`: ReactNode — Label content. Never put interactive elements here.
- `side / align`: "top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left" / "start" | "center" | "end" (default "top" / "center") — Anchor side and cross-axis alignment.
- `delay`: number (default 150) — Hover open delay in ms. Keyboard focus opens instantly.
- `followCursor`: boolean (default false) — Label trails the pointer with drift-damped lag; leader line omitted.
- `disabled`: boolean (default false) — Never opens.

Notes:
- Opens on hover and on keyboard focus; Escape dismisses.
- Under reduced motion the card fades in place — no pop, no leader draw, and followCursor pins to the anchor.

### Morph Dialog (KQ-009) — `morph-dialog`
The trigger becomes the dialog.

The trigger becomes the dialog — a shared-element morph glides the card you clicked into the panel it opens, and reverses on close.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/morph-dialog`

Props:
- `open / defaultOpen / onOpenChange`: boolean / boolean / (open) => void — Controlled or uncontrolled open state.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — Panel width preset; ignored by the sheet variant.
- `sheet`: boolean (default false) — Bottom-sheet variant — full-width, pinned to the bottom edge.
- `dismissible`: boolean (default true) — Escape, backdrop click, and the built-in close button.
- `portal`: boolean (default true) — Portal to body, or contain the overlay in a relative parent.
- `Content.title / Content.description`: string — Wired to aria-labelledby and aria-describedby; title renders as h2.

Notes:
- Focus is trapped while open and restored to the trigger on close; body scroll locks in portal mode.
- Under reduced motion the morph becomes a plain centered fade.

### Select (KQ-010) — `select`
A menu that unfolds from where you asked.

A menu that unfolds from where you asked — the panel scales from the trigger's edge, options cascade in, and a highlight bar glides between them.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/select`

Props:
- `items`: (SelectOption | SelectGroup)[] — Flat options, labeled groups, or a mix; options take value, label, description, disabled.
- `value / defaultValue / onValueChange`: string / string / (value) => void — Controlled or uncontrolled selection.
- `searchable`: boolean (default false) — Pins a filter input at the top of the panel.
- `placeholder / label / name`: string — Empty-state text, wired visible label, and hidden form input.

Notes:
- Combobox APG throughout: aria-activedescendant highlight, wrapping arrows, typeahead, Escape restores focus.
- Under reduced motion everything fades — no scale, no cascade, instant highlight bar.

### Telemetry Toast (KQ-011) — `telemetry-toast`
Messages that queue like readings.

Messages that queue like readings — recoil arrivals, a depth-receding stack, swipe dismissal with velocity projection, and timers that pause under your pointer.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/telemetry-toast`

Props:
- `ToastProvider.position`: "bottom-right" | "bottom-left" | "top-right" | "top-left" (default "bottom-right") — Viewport corner for the stack.
- `ToastProvider.max`: number (default 3) — Visible stack size; extras queue FIFO.
- `useToast()`: { toast(input) => id, dismiss(id) } — Imperative API from anywhere under the provider.
- `ToastInput`: title, description?, variant?, duration?, action? — Variants info | success | warn | danger; duration ≤ 0 persists; action renders a button.

Notes:
- Danger toasts announce as alerts; the region is focusable via an Alt+T hotkey chord and timers pause on hover or focus.
- Under reduced motion the stack flattens to a list with fade-only transitions — the progress hairline still drains.

### Readout (KQ-012) — `readout`
Numbers with momentum.

Numbers with momentum — per-digit vertical rolls with real carry propagation, so 199 → 200 visibly carries right to left.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/readout`

Props:
- `value`: number — The numeric value to display.
- `format`: (value: number) => string (default toLocaleString) — Formats the value; non-digit characters render as static cells.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" (default "md") — Type scale.
- `rollOn`: "any" | "increase" (default "any") — With "increase", decreases swap instantly — right for latency-style metrics.
- `delta`: { value: string; direction: "up" | "down" } — Change badge that flips up when the value moves.

Notes:
- Rolling digits are aria-hidden; a polite live region announces the settled value once per burst.
- Under reduced motion the value swaps instantly with a brief highlight pulse.

### Focus Text (KQ-013) — `focus-text`
Copy that resolves under the lens.

Copy that resolves under the lens — words sharpen from an 8px blur like a microscope focus-pull, cascaded under the 600ms budget.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/focus-text`

Props:
- `children`: string — The copy to resolve.
- `as`: "span" | "div" | "p" | "h1"–"h4" (default "span") — Rendered element.
- `by`: "word" | "char" (default "word") — Split granularity; char mode never breaks mid-word.
- `trigger / once`: "inView" | "mount" / boolean (default "inView" / true) — When the pull runs, and whether it re-blurs out of view.
- `stagger / startDelay`: number — Seconds between units (defaults to the cascade budget) and lead-in delay.

Notes:
- Screen readers get a clean sr-only copy; the animated units are aria-hidden.
- Under reduced motion the block does a single fast fade — text is always readable.

### Flapboard (KQ-014) — `flapboard`
Split-flap departures for your data.

Split-flap departures for your data — each cell flips through intermediate characters with a column cascade, like an airport board settling.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/flapboard`

Props:
- `value`: string — Text to display, normalized against the charset.
- `chars`: string (default " A–Z 0–9 ·-") — Charset scanned in flip order.
- `flipSpeed`: number (default 40) — Milliseconds per flip step.
- `padTo / align`: number / "left" | "right" — Minimum cell count and which side the value sits on.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — Fixed tile dimensions.

Notes:
- Cells are aria-hidden; a polite status region announces the settled value once.
- Under reduced motion the board crossfades to the new value — no flipping.

### Scope Scrubber (KQ-015) — `scope-scrubber`
Drag a value; watch its physics.

Drag a value; watch its physics — a scrub input with a live oscilloscope trace behind the numeral, where the settle spring's overshoot draws itself.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/scope-scrubber`

Props:
- `min / max / step`: number — Bounds (required) and release snap grid.
- `value / defaultValue / onValueChange`: number / number / (value) => void — Controlled or uncontrolled; fires live while scrubbing.
- `settle`: SpringName (default "snap") — Which calibrated spring the value settles on — its personality shows on the trace.
- `sensitivity`: number (default (max−min)/200) — Value change per pixel of drag.
- `label / unit / format / trace`: string / string / (v)=>string / boolean — Labeling, suffix, numeral formatting, and the history trace toggle.

Notes:
- Enter or double-click converts the plate into a plain number input; Escape cancels.
- Under reduced motion scrubbing stays 1:1, release snaps instantly, and the trace hides.

### Metronome Loader (KQ-016) — `metronome-loader`
Waiting, kept honest.

Waiting, kept honest — a pendulum, a bearing cradle, or a radar sweep; give it a value and it morphs into a determinate arc gauge.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/metronome-loader`

Props:
- `variant`: "pendulum" | "bearing" | "sweep" (default "pendulum") — Indeterminate style; ignored once value is set.
- `size`: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default "md") — 24 / 40 / 64 px.
- `value`: number — 0–100; presence morphs the loader into a determinate arc gauge.
- `label / showLabel`: string / boolean — Accessible name; optionally rendered visibly.

Notes:
- role="progressbar" throughout — indeterminate announces Loading, determinate reports its value.
- Under reduced motion the loops freeze to a static glyph with a slow opacity pulse.

### Gyro Card (KQ-017) — `gyro-card`
A card with a sense of balance.

A card with a sense of balance — pointer tilt with real inertia that overshoots past level and rebalances when you leave, with layered parallax and tracking glare.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/gyro-card`

Props:
- `maxTilt`: number (default 8) — Peak rotation toward the pointer, in degrees.
- `glare`: boolean (default true) — Radial sheen that tracks the light angle.
- `GyroLayer.depth`: 0 | 1 | 2 — Parallax depth for child slots — pinned, ±4px, or ±8px counter-translation.

Notes:
- The motion is decorative: DOM order is untouched, and keyboard focus inside flattens the card to an energized ring state.
- Under reduced motion there is no tilt, parallax, or glare — hover becomes a border emphasis.

### Magnet Dock (KQ-018) — `magnet-dock`
Icons that feel the cursor coming.

Icons that feel the cursor coming — a cosine distance field magnifies the dock, and drag-reorder parts neighbors magnetically before snapping into a slot.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/magnet-dock`

Props:
- `items`: DockItem[] — { id, label, icon, active?, onSelect? } per icon.
- `orientation`: "horizontal" | "vertical" (default "horizontal") — Dock axis — pointer tracking, tooltips, and arrows follow.
- `magnify`: number (default 1.6) — Peak scale under the pointer or keyboard focus.
- `reorderable / onReorder`: boolean / (order: string[]) => void — Pointer drag plus Space-lift keyboard reordering, announced live.

Notes:
- role="toolbar" with roving tabindex; a focused icon magnifies without the pointer.
- Under reduced motion magnification is replaced by a 2px raise; reordering still works, 1:1.

### Conveyor List (KQ-019) — `conveyor-list`

A queue that moves like a belt — items drift in from the feed side, brake into their slot with a squash, and lift off the belt when removed.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/conveyor-list`

Props:
- `items / keyFor / renderItem`: T[] / (item) => string / (item) => ReactNode — Generic queue contents with stable keys driving enter, exit, and reorder identity.
- `side`: "top" | "bottom" (default "top") — The feed edge new items enter from.
- `maxVisible`: number (default 6) — Rows shown before the oldest overflow into a +N more count.
- `announceItem`: (item: T) => string — Screen-reader text per row for the live log region.

Notes:
- The list is a role="log" live region — arrivals are announced politely.
- Under reduced motion rows crossfade in place and layout shifts are instant.

### Scan Reveal (KQ-021) — `scan-reveal`
Sections develop as the scanner passes.

Sections develop as the scanner passes — a scroll-linked scan line sweeps once, and content resolves beneath it with a coordinate readout riding the beam.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/scan-reveal`

Props:
- `once`: boolean (default true) — Tear down the dual layers after the sweep completes.
- `direction`: "down" | "up" (default "down") — Sweep direction.
- `containerRef`: RefObject<HTMLElement> — Scrollable ancestor for scroll-linking inside overflow containers.

Notes:
- Interactive content lives only in the developed layer; the undeveloped copy is aria-hidden and inert.
- A containerRef must point at a positioned element — progress is measured through the offsetParent chain, so a static container never sweeps.
- Under reduced motion content renders fully developed with a single fast fade.

### Code Cells (KQ-023) — `code-cells`
Six digits, dropped into place.

Six digits, dropped into place — one hidden one-time-code input drives visual cells with digit drops, underline ticks, and a rejection nudge.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/code-cells`

Props:
- `length`: number (default 6) — Cell count; also the hidden input's maxLength.
- `value / defaultValue / onValueChange`: string / string / (code) => void — Controlled or uncontrolled code, digits only.
- `onComplete`: (code: string) => void — Fires once per fill; re-arms when the code shrinks.
- `error / errorMessage`: boolean / string — Destructive borders plus a row nudge and a role=alert line.
- `groups`: number[] — e.g. [3,3] renders a separator between digit groups.
- `ref`: Ref<HTMLInputElement> — Reaches the hidden input — focus() after clearing.

Notes:
- The single hidden input with autocomplete="one-time-code" is the accessibility-correct OTP pattern — cells are decorative.
- Under reduced motion digits appear instantly and the nudge is skipped; the alert still announces.

### Action Relay (KQ-024) — `action-relay`
A button that narrates the job.

A button that narrates the job — state labels roll through a one-line mask with a blur crossfade while the width follows the new content.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/action-relay`

Props:
- `state / states`: string / Record<string, ReactNode> — Controlled state key and the content per state — nodes may embed icons or a small loader.
- `busyStates`: string[] — States that report aria-busy and suppress interaction without stealing focus.
- `onSettled`: (state) => void — Fires when the incoming roll lands — chain done → idle off it.
- `announcements`: Record<string, string> — Screen-reader text per state; plain-text nodes announce themselves.
- `variant / size`: pressure-button scales (default "solid" / "md") — Visual style, mirroring the button family.

Notes:
- Busy states keep focus (aria-disabled, not disabled) so the announcement chain is never interrupted.
- Under reduced motion labels crossfade and the width jumps; onSettled still fires.

### Status Seal (KQ-025) — `status-seal`
Status, re-stamped on every change.

A face-on pile of layers browsed along the z-axis — scroll a notch, drag, or arrow through; the active layer sits crisp while the rest recede into a stepped skyline of peeking headers.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/depth-stack`

Props:
- `layers`: { id, label, content }[] — Three to eight layers, front to deepest.
- `index / defaultIndex / onIndexChange`: number / number / (index) => void — Controlled or uncontrolled active layer; fires once per settle.
- `height`: number (default 260) — Stage height in px.
- `aria-label`: string — Required — names the layer stack.

Notes:
- Arrows and the wheel move one layer, Home and End jump on the glide spring, tick-rail buttons carry aria-current, and settles are announced.
- Under reduced motion the active layer renders alone beneath a compressed label shelf with instant swaps.

### Peek Portal (KQ-062) — `peek-portal`

- `sceneLabel / backLabel`: string / string — Accessible names for the frame button and the back chip.

Notes:

- Under reduced motion there is no parallax and both steps are instant crossfades.

- Eye-tracking only engages for a fine pointer; touch just boops.
- Under reduced motion it still boops the face and cheeks but skips the squash and the eye spring.

A trigger-anchored menu that unfolds from its button on a single crisp overshoot, a small arrow tracking the trigger. - `align`: start | end — Preferred horizontal edge; flips on overflow.
- `label`: string — Accessible name for the menu surface.

- Under reduced motion it appears without the unfold or the row cascade.

### Volley Thread (KQ-211) — `volley-thread`
Each turn lands under its own weight.

A conversation where each turn arrives under its own weight. - Under reduced motion the travel is dropped and turns resolve in place.

### Prompt Well (KQ-212) — `prompt-well`
Deepens as the thought gets longer.

A composer that deepens as the thought gets longer, growing line by line to a row cap and then holding and scrolling so the send control never walks down the page. Typing @ opens the sources it can draw on and / opens the commands it can run, filtered as you type; the list rises on snap, arrow keys move, Enter or Tab takes one. The field is a combobox over that list with an active descendant, so the highlighted row is announced without the caret leaving the text.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/prompt-well`

Props:
- `attachments / onAttach / onRemoveAttachment`: WellAttachment[] · () => void · (id: string) => void — A chip row above the field and a paperclip in the tool row; all optional.
- `queued / credits`: string[] · { used: number; limit: number; label?: string } — Messages waiting while busy, and a small usage pill in the tool row.
- `sources`: WellOption[] — Offered after @, anywhere a word can start.
- `commands`: WellOption[] — Offered after /, and only when it leads the prompt.
- `busy`: boolean — Swaps send for stop and blocks submission.
- `maxRows`: number — Rows the well grows to before it scrolls.
- `models / model / onModelChange`: string[] · string · (model) => void — A cycling model chip in the footer — the current choice is always printed, never hidden in a menu.
- `onDictate`: () => void — Offers a dictation control beside send; the well never records audio itself.
- `shape`: "well" | "pill" (default "well") — The container silhouette.

Notes:
- A trigger only counts at the start of a word and a space closes it, so prose never opens the list.
- Enter sends and Shift+Enter breaks the line; Escape dismisses the list without clearing the field.
- Under reduced motion the list appears in place and the control swaps without travel.

### Code Lathe (KQ-213) — `code-lathe`
Turned out one line at a time.

A listing turned out line by line, the way an agent actually writes one — each line landing a beat behind the one above so the block builds at a readable pace instead of appearing whole. Highlighting is a single deterministic pass over comments, strings, numbers, and words: enough to read a snippet by, with no parser and nothing to load. In diff mode a leading plus or minus becomes a gutter marker and a tinted row, and is stripped from what gets copied.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/code-lathe`

Props:
- `code`: string — The source to display.
- `stream`: boolean — Turn the listing out line by line instead of whole.
- `diff`: boolean — Read a leading +/- as an edit and mark the gutter.
- `perLine`: number — Seconds per line while streaming.

Notes:
- Every line is in the DOM from the first frame and only dimmed while it waits, so copy and screen readers always see the whole source.
- Highlighting is regex-only and language-agnostic; it never ships a grammar or a worker.
- Under reduced motion the listing is simply there, complete and still.

### Work Lamp (KQ-214) — `work-lamp`
A wait with a clock on it is a report.

The lamp that says the bench is busy: one of four honest faces — a shimmering pixel grid, breathing dots, an orbiting pair, a sweeping bar — beside the work's name and a ticking elapsed readout. A wait with a clock on it is a report; a wait without one is a hope. Time starts at mount, never the wall clock at render, so server and client always agree.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/work-lamp`

Props:
- `face`: "grid" | "orbit" | "dots" | "sweep" (default "grid") — Which lamp is lit.
- `label`: string — What the bench is doing, in a word or two.
- `elapsed`: number — Externally-owned seconds; omit and the lamp keeps time from mount.
- `showElapsed`: boolean (default true) — Show the ticking readout beside the label.

Notes:
- The elapsed numeral is plain tabular figures, not a rolling readout — at ten ticks a second a carry-roll is noise.
- Under reduced motion the faces hold still but the clock keeps ticking: elapsed time is information, not decoration.
- aria-live is off by design; a loader that announces every tick talks over the answer it precedes.

### Train of Thought (KQ-215) — `train-of-thought`
Reasoning available, never performed.

The agent's working shown as a trace: a quiet summary chip — Thought for 4 seconds — that opens into the steps it actually took, cascading in as plain clauses, searches with hit counts, and mono tool lines. The chip is the honest default: reasoning is available, never performed at the reader, and the active step carries a breathing marker so a live trace reads as live.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/train-of-thought`

Props:
- `summary`: string — The chip line, e.g. "Thought for 4 seconds".
- `steps`: ThoughtStep[] — The trace: plain steps, searches with counts, mono code lines; one may be active.
- `open / defaultOpen / onOpenChange`: boolean · (open) => void — Controlled or uncontrolled disclosure.

Notes:
- Default closed on purpose — the trace is for the reader who asks, not a performance for everyone.
- Mark at most one step active; its breathing dot is what makes a live trace read as live.
- Under reduced motion the drawer opens instantly and steps print in place.

### Source Stream (KQ-216) — `source-stream`
Provenance at the point of assertion.

An answer that streams in with its sources landing inline: prose arrives word by word, and when a claim finishes, its citation chip drops into the sentence right where the claim was made — provenance at the point of assertion, not footnoted at the end. A sources tray sums the run, and follow-up asks appear only once the stream is done.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/source-stream`

Props:
- `segments`: StreamSegment[] — The answer in claim-sized pieces; a segment's source chip lands when its words finish.
- `followUps / onFollowUp`: string[] · (text) => void — Suggested next asks, offered after completion.
- `rate`: number (default 14) — Words per second while streaming.
- `immediate`: boolean — Print whole at once (reduced motion forces this too).

Notes:
- The stream is a mount-driven tick, never the wall clock — a re-render never re-streams.
- The live region announces once, at completion; a per-word live region reads the answer out dozens of times.
- Segment at claim boundaries: the chip belongs to the sentence that needed it.

### Countersign (KQ-217) — `countersign`
Asked before acting, never after.

The questions an agent asks before it acts, paged one at a time: pick an option, then press Continue — picking never advances on its own, because a card that moves the moment you touch it cannot be reconsidered, and these are precisely the decisions that deserve a second look. Skip is always offered; a human-in-the-loop card that cannot be declined is a form wearing a question's clothes.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/countersign`

Props:
- `questions`: CountersignQuestion[] — Each with a prompt and its option pills; answered as a radiogroup.
- `onComplete`: (answers) => void — Fired once at the end; skipped questions are absent from the record.
- `heading / skipLabel / continueLabel / doneLine`: string — The card's fixed copy.

Notes:
- Selection never auto-advances — Continue is the countersignature.
- Skip is per-question and honest: a skipped answer is absent, not defaulted.
- The finished card reads back every decision, so the sign-off is inspectable after the fact.

### Tool Trace (KQ-218) — `tool-trace`
The run at chip height.

A tool run folded into a chip: collapsed, one line says what happened — 4 tool calls, 2 messages — and open, the run replays as its parts: a thinking note, a code write on the lathe, a command with its checks printing, a read with what was seen. File-change chips close the run with +/− counts and an honest overflow. The point is proportion: agents work loudly, and a transcript that prints every tool call at full height buries the answer the run was for.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/tool-trace`

Props:
- `calls`: ToolCall[] — Thinking, write, run, and read parts, in order.
- `changes / maxChanges`: FileChange[] · number — File chips with +/− counts; the rest fold into +N more.
- `summary / defaultOpen`: string · boolean — The collapsed line, and whether the run starts open.

Notes:
- The code write composes code-lathe (whole, diff gutters on), so the snippet is copyable and complete for assistive tech from first paint.
- Collapsed is the honest default — the answer matters more than the machinery that fetched it.
- The overflow count is real: chips beyond maxChanges are counted, never dropped silently.

### Run Sheet (KQ-219) — `run-sheet`
Failures shown, not folded in.

The agent's task list as a working document: parent tasks carrying a rolling count, child rows carrying their own verdicts — done ticks, a breathing running dot, failures shown red rather than folded into a success number. Two faces: capsules for a panel, a flat list for a transcript. Statuses are carried by word and mark together, never by colour alone.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/run-sheet`

Props:
- `tasks`: RunTask[] — Parents with counts and their child items, each with a status.
- `face`: "capsule" | "list" (default "capsule") — Capsule cards for a panel, a flat rail for a transcript.

Notes:
- Counts roll on the readout — they are the part that changes while you watch.
- A failed child stays red under a done parent; hiding it inside an aggregate is how trust is lost.
- Every status is announced by word for screen readers; the mark alone is never the message.

### Counsel Card (KQ-220) — `counsel-card`
Sureness stated, or nothing.

One suggestion, offered rather than executed: the counsel in a sentence with its subject carried as a chip, an honest tri-state confidence meter — high, needs review, no signal — and the alternatives kept a fold away with their own confidence attached. The meter is the card's spine: a recommendation that cannot say how sure it is will be trusted exactly once.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/counsel-card`

Props:
- `counsel / subject`: string — The sentence and the entity chip carried inside it.
- `confidence`: "high" | "review" | "none" — The tri-state meter — bars and words together.
- `alternatives`: CounselAlternative[] — Each with its own confidence, kept a fold away.
- `onAccept`: () => void — Fired once; accepting seals the card so nothing executes twice.

Notes:
- Alternatives carry their own meters — a list of options without confidence is a menu, not counsel.
- Accepting seals the card in place; the accepted state reads back what happened.
- The meter pairs bars with words, so confidence is never carried by colour alone.

### Source Shelf (KQ-221) — `source-shelf`
What the model was given, on the shelf.

The retrieved context, shelved in plain sight: each chunk carries its title, the excerpt itself, a character count, and the document it came from typed by kind — so what the model was given is inspectable, not implied. The count header admits how much of the working set is off-shelf. An answer's context is part of the answer; a system that hides its retrieval asks to be trusted twice.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/source-shelf`

Props:
- `chunks`: ShelfChunk[] — Title, excerpt, pre-counted characters, and a typed source document.
- `total`: number — The full working set, including chunks not shown.

Notes:
- Character counts are pre-counted data, not derived from the excerpt — the excerpt is a cut, the count is the whole.
- State the off-shelf remainder via total; a shelf that looks complete when it is not is a quiet lie.
- Source kind chips are text, not icons, so a new file type needs no asset.

### Redline Table (KQ-222) — `redline-table`
A per-row veto on wholesale edits.

An agent's proposed edits laid over the table itself: removals struck through, additions tinted in, changes shown as was and would-be — and every proposal is a toggle, so the reader accepts or declines row by row before anything is applied. The counts under the grid derive from what is currently accepted; the apply button never claims more than the toggles say.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/redline-table`

Props:
- `rows`: RedlineRow[] — Cells plus a kind — keep, remove, add, or change with its next cells.
- `onApply`: (acceptedIds) => void — Fired once with only the rows still accepted.
- `applyLabel`: (count) => string — The button copy, given the live accepted count.

Notes:
- Proposals start accepted; a click withdraws one. The counts and the button derive from the toggles, never from the proposal.
- Changed rows show both readings — was struck through, would-be beneath — so a change is never a mystery diff.
- Applying seals the table; nothing can be applied twice.

### Sieve Table (KQ-223) — `sieve-table`
Surviving rows glide; hidden ones are counted.

A table sieved by status chips: pick a chip and the rows that survive glide to their new positions while the rest fold away — a layout move, never a reprint, because rows that teleport can't be followed and rows that reprint can't be trusted to be the same rows. Every chip carries its count, derived from the data, so the filter admits how much it hides.

Notes:
- The chips are a real radiogroup; All is a first-class member, not an absence of filter.
- Chip counts derive from the rows, so the filter admits what it hides.
- Under reduced motion rows fade in place rather than travel.

### Contact Ledger (KQ-224) — `contact-ledger`

A relationship grid that reads like a book: records grouped under alphabetical rails, each row carrying its tags, a pre-formatted last-touch date, and a three-bar strength meter labelled in words. Notes:
- For working ten thousand rows, reach for the ledger — this one is for reading a hundred relationships honestly.
- Strength pairs bars with words; the meter is never colour alone.
- Dates are pre-formatted strings, so the grid never reads a clock and cannot drift from the server.

Notes:
- Stamp order, rotation, and color all cycle from fixed arrays — no randomness, identical replay.
- Clear fades the sheet with a cascade stagger; the cap clear happens before the next stamp lands.
- Reduced motion places stamps at rest instantly, no ring, instant clear.

### Cookie Bite (KQ-251) — `cookie-bite`
Five bites, no regrets, free refills.

A cookie you eat one click at a time: five bites disappear from the rim in a fixed order through an SVG mask, each with a startle squash and three crumbs arcing to the plate. When it is gone, the plate admits “worth it” — and a fresh one springs in, because grief should be brief.

- A polite live region counts the bites for screen readers.
- Reduced motion swaps the mask instantly — no crumbs, no squash, instant refill.

### Dodge Button (KQ-283) — `dodge-button`
Two dodges, then it gives up.

A button that plays hard to get exactly twice, then relents — approach it with a pointer and it springs to the next seat in a fixed cycle, and after two dodges it returns to centre and lets you click it. Keyboard users are never dodged, and neither are touch devices, because a button that runs away from a thumb is not a joke, it is a bug.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/dodge-button`

Props:
- `label`: string (default "Delete everything") — What the button claims it will do.
- `dodges`: number (default 2) — Evasions before it relents (0–4).

Notes:
- Keyboard focus and Enter or Space never trigger a dodge — the bit is pointer-only, by design.
- Coarse pointers are exempt entirely; the button simply works on touch.
- Reduced motion skips the bit and presents a normal button from the start.

### Oracle Orb (KQ-284) — `oracle-orb`
Ask again Monday.

A fortune-telling orb with the mysticism removed: shake it and the fluid clouds, the die surfaces, and an answer fades in that sounds like it came from a colleague rather than a spirit. Answers cycle in fixed order, so a demo tells everyone the same fortunes in the same sequence — which is the only honest way to run an oracle.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/oracle-orb`

Props:
- `answers`: string[] — Override the built-in eight; they cycle in order.
- `onAnswer`: (answer: string) => void — Fires with each surfaced answer.

Notes:
- Re-shaking mid-answer restarts the sequence rather than queueing — that is how the real object behaves.
- The mist is layered translucent gradients, not a blur filter, so it stays cheap.
- Reduced motion swaps straight to the next answer with the die at rest.

### Mood Gem (KQ-285) — `mood-gem`
It can tell how you are moving.

A faceted gem that reads the room from how you move: quick passes make it restless, slow ones calm it, sitting still turns it content, and leaving makes it still. It rotates almost imperceptibly so the facets keep catching differently, and clicking sets the current mood for a few seconds regardless of what your hands do next.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/mood-gem`

Props:
- `onMood`: (mood: string) => void — Fires when the mood changes.

Notes:
- Mood is bucketed from speed and dwell, and state only changes when the bucket does — never per pointer move.
- The idle rotation is deliberately too slow to notice directly; you only see that the light has changed.
- Reduced motion drops the rotation and pulse, keeping instant colour changes and the caption.

### Disco Floor (KQ-286) — `disco-floor`
It dances when you look away.

A small dance floor that lights under your cursor with a soft falloff and, left alone for a moment, starts dancing on its own through authored patterns — sweeps, checkers, a pulse from the centre. Move back in and it yields to you immediately. Clicking drops a beat: everything flashes, then falls back in a cascade.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/disco-floor`

Props:
- `onBeat`: () => void — Fires on the beat drop.

Notes:
- This is a lighting toy on a fixed grid, not a layout — reach for the tile grid when you need to arrange content.
- Idle frames are an authored table, so the floor performs the same routine everywhere.
- Reduced motion leaves the floor dark until hovered and drops the idle routine entirely.

### Drum Pads (KQ-287) — `drum-pads`
Visual instruments. Loud anyway.

Four squashy pads that hit like the real thing: each squashes under the strike and throws a burst matched to its voice — a thick ring for the kick, sharp lines for the snare, a fine spray for the hat, staggered arcs for the clap. Hit one repeatedly and the bursts grow. A strip beneath keeps the last eight hits, so you can see the groove you just played.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/drum-pads`

Props:
- `onHit`: (pad: string) => void — Fires with the struck pad's name.

Notes:
- A, S, D, F play the pads when the group has focus, so a rhythm can be played with both hands.
- Repeat hits build a streak that grows the burst, decaying after a short pause — velocity you can see.
- Reduced motion flashes the pad and still records the mark, with no squash or burst.

### Snow Shake (KQ-288) — `snow-shake`
Shake it. Then watch it settle.

A snow globe you shake by click or by drag, where the settling is the point: flakes lift off the drift, swirl on seeded paths, and come down staggered until the last one lands and the caption says so. Every flake's path is derived from its index, so the same shake happens for everyone — a snow globe with no randomness in it at all.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/snow-shake`

Props:
- `flakes`: number (default 14) — Flakes in the dome (6–24).
- `onSettle`: () => void — Fires when the last flake lands.

Notes:
- Drag energy scales the rock and the swirl duration — a hard shake really does snow longer.
- Flake paths come from seeded per-index constants, never a random source.
- Reduced motion redistributes the flakes and settles them in two instant steps.

### Zen Rake (KQ-289) — `zen-rake`
Three grooves that heal themselves.

A sand garden and a three-tooth comb: drag and three parallel grooves follow your hand, offset along the path normal so the rake reads as a rake. Strokes rest for a few seconds and then heal, the bed holding only its last six so it never silts up. Arrow keys rake too, for anyone gardening from the keyboard.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/zen-rake`

Props:
- `onStroke`: (count: number) => void — Fires per completed stroke.

Notes:
- Points are only recorded every few pixels, so a long drag stays cheap and the curve stays smooth.
- Strokes cap at six and heal on a timer — the bed is self-cleaning by design.
- Reduced motion draws grooves at full opacity and removes them outright instead of fading.

### Wind Chimes (KQ-290) — `wind-chimes`
Still, breath, gust, squall.

Five graduated tubes that sway from the breeze your cursor makes, each on its own natural period so they never move in unison — that desync is the entire effect. Contacts with the clapper flash in sequence rather than at once, and a click plays a full run down the scale. The caption names the weather you are making.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/wind-chimes`

Props:
- `onRing`: () => void — Fires on a full run.

Notes:
- Breeze is bucketed into four states; only a bucket change restarts the sways, never a pointer move.
- Contacts come from fixed per-tube phases rather than collision maths — cheaper, and it reads better.
- Reduced motion hangs the tubes still, keeps the weather caption, and brightens them in sequence on click.

### Ferris Glow (KQ-291) — `ferris-glow`
The cabins stay level. That is the trick.

A little ferris wheel turning at dusk, with the detail that matters: the cabins counter-rotate so they stay level however far the wheel has come around. Cabin and rim lights pulse on offset phases so the whole thing twinkles instead of blinking, hovering speeds the turn, and a click lights every bulb at once before they settle back in a cascade.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/ferris-glow`

Props:
- `cabins`: number (default 8) — Cabins on the rim (6–12).
- `onLight`: () => void — Fires when every bulb lights.

Notes:
- One shared transform counter-rotates every cabin — one hook, reused, regardless of cabin count.
- Rim positions are index maths, so the wheel is identical on server and client.
- Reduced motion parks the wheel at a pleasing angle with lights at mid brightness.

### Sky Bloom (KQ-292) — `sky-bloom`
Tap the sky. Mind the gravity.

Fireworks you set off yourself: click anywhere in the night sky and a rocket rises from the skyline beneath your finger, decelerating to apex before blooming into twelve sparks that arc and droop under authored gravity. Three may be in the air at once, palettes cycle so consecutive shots differ, and the sky brightens a touch with each one.

### Mail Fold (KQ-293) — `mail-fold`
It folds, it seals, it goes.

A letter that folds itself into an envelope and leaves: the bottom third comes up, the top third comes down, a flap sweeps over, a seal presses on, and the whole thing tilts off the top-right corner trailing a dash of its own path. A fresh sheet drops in behind it. For sent-confirmations that deserve more than a checkmark.

### Fridge Poetry (KQ-294) — `fridge-poetry`
Ten words. No wrong answers.

Word magnets on a fridge door, draggable into whatever sentence you like — each lands on a loose grid with a small jiggle that sells the weight of the magnet, and the one you touched last sits on top. - Landing snaps to a 12px grid — loose enough to feel hand-placed, tight enough to line up.

### Juggle Loop (KQ-295) — `juggle-loop`
Three, then four, then dropped.

Three balls in a proper cascade, each on the same authored arc offset by a third of the cycle, with hands that dip as they catch. Click to add a ball up to five — the tempo tightens to keep it plausible — and one more click drops the lot before starting over. Hovering runs it in slow motion, which is when you can see the pattern.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/juggle-loop`

Props:
- `balls`: number (default 3) — Starting count (3–5).
- `onDrop`: () => void — Fires when the pattern collapses.

Notes:
- Every ball runs the same keyframe arc with a phase delay — no per-ball hooks, so the count is free to change.
- Hover scales the durations rather than restarting the loop, so slow motion never resets the pattern.
- Reduced motion arranges the balls in a still tableau and keeps the counting.

### Rocket Drill (KQ-296) — `rocket-drill`
Three, two, one, and back again.

A launch with a countdown and, unusually, a recovery: three numerals pop while the rocket trembles harder, the gantry swings clear, it climbs out of frame on smoke, and then a parachute drifts the capsule back down to the pad. Most launch animations forget the coming-back part, which is the half that makes it a drill.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/rocket-drill`

- `onLaunch / onRecover`: () => void · () => void — Fires at liftoff, and again on landing.

Notes:
- The tremble escalates per count — the suspense is built from the same jitter at three amplitudes.
- Every chained beat is a tracked timer, so an unmount mid-drill leaves nothing running.
- Reduced motion steps the stills: pad, countdown, empty sky, parachute, landed.

- Reduced motion parks the trolley and cycles through the remaining plushes so the toy still progresses.

### Quest Log (KQ-298) — `quest-log`
Finishing one opens the next.

A quest list built to be finished: each advance rolls its counter and fills its bar, and completing one sweeps the row, flies its reward to the running total, and unlocks the next quest in the chain. The unlock is the hook — a log that opens its own next line is harder to close than one that simply ends.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/quest-log`

Notes:
- Rewards fly to the header total, which carries on the house readout — the same roll every number in the system uses.
- Locked rows are genuinely inert; the chain only opens as its predecessor closes.
- Reduced motion drops the sweeps and flights but keeps every state legible.

### Skill Tree (KQ-299) — `skill-tree`
Spend a point, open two doors.

A talent tree you spend points into: available nodes pulse for attention, spending one fills the node, draws the link from its parent, and cascades any newly-eligible node into reach. The capstone sweeps the whole tree. Respec drains it all back in reverse, because a build you cannot undo is a build nobody experiments with.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/skill-tree`

- `points`: number (default 3) — Points available to spend.
- `onUnlock`: (id: string) => void — Fires per node owned.

Notes:
- The layout is an authored table in a fixed viewBox — nothing is measured, so the tree is identical on server and client.
- Links draw with pathLength as the tree grows and undraw on respec.
- Reduced motion swaps node states and shows links complete, with no pulses or draws.

Let it empty and the combo shatters, the panel cools, and your best score stays on screen as the reason to go again.

- Reduced motion steps the bar in visible increments instead of draining continuously.

- Reduced motion claims instantly and keeps the totals and captions.

### Timing Bar (KQ-313) — `timing-bar`
Stop it in the narrow band.

The bar every crafting game teaches you to hit: a marker sweeps, you stop it, and the hit-test reads the marker's live motion value rather than any state — which is what makes the judgement honest. The perfect zone sits deliberately off-centre so it has to be learned, and every success speeds the next sweep while narrowing the target.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/timing-bar`

Props:
- `onResult`: (result: "perfect" | "good" | "miss") => void — Fires per attempt with the judgement.

Notes:
- The judgement reads the live motion value in the handler — never state, which would lag a frame and lie.
- A miss resets both the streak and the difficulty; the loss has to be legible or the streak means nothing.
- Reduced motion steps the marker in discrete positions so the skill check survives without continuous motion.

Notes:
- Judgement is step arithmetic off an interval counter — no wall clock, no DOM measurement.
- It starts paused by design; an autoplaying rhythm lane in a docs page is a nuisance.
- Reduced motion pulses the hit zone on the beat instead of travelling notes.

A ring shrinking toward a target you tap when they match — and then it tells you the signed error in pixels, so you learn whether you are early or late. That readout is the whole teaching device. Success speeds the next ring and narrows the band; a miss resets both.

### Power Gauge (KQ-316) — `power-gauge`
Max power is the trap.

Hold to charge, release to commit — and the needle does not stop at full, it oscillates, so overcharging is a real risk and waiting for the second pass is a real strategy. The sweet spot sits below maximum on purpose: max power is a trap, and the overcharge result is visibly worse than a good one.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/power-gauge`

Props:
- `onShot`: (result: "weak" | "good" | "sweet" | "over", value: number) => void — Fires on release with the band and the value.

Notes:
- The release reads the needle's live motion value; a release always lands even if the pointer left the button.
- The best marker stays pinned on the result bar — chasing your own best is the loop.
- Reduced motion steps the needle on an interval while held, judging identically.

### Reflex Light (KQ-317) — `reflex-light`
Jump the start and it does not count.

Five lights arm one at a time, hold, and go out together — that blackout is the signal. Timing comes from event timestamps, never the wall clock, and a click before the lights drop is a jump start that voids the attempt. The penalty is what makes the wait tense.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/reflex-light`

Props:
- `delays`: number[] — The hold before the lights drop, cycled in fixed order — reproducible, and learnable.
- `onReaction`: (ms: number) => void — Fires with the measured reaction.

Notes:
- Delays cycle a fixed table rather than rolling — a practised user can learn it, which is the fair price of reproducibility.
- Every pending timer is cleared on a jump start, a reset, and unmount.
- Reduced motion keeps the sequence — it is discrete state — and drops only the sparks and flashes.

### Energy Pips (KQ-318) — `energy-pips`
The wait is the mechanic. Say so.

The energy economy that decides when someone comes back: pips drain as they are spent and refill on a timer that only runs while the bank is below full. At zero the wait is stated plainly rather than hidden, because an honest countdown is the mechanic. Nothing here reads the wall clock — the countdown is an interval tick counter, so it renders the same on the server.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/energy-pips`

Props:
- `max / start`: number · number (default 6 · 4) — Bank size and opening balance.
- `refillSeconds`: number (default 6) — Seconds per regenerated pip.

Notes:
- The refill timer stops at full — a topped-up bank should not keep ticking.
- The empty state names the wait instead of just disabling the button.
- Reduced motion swaps pip states instantly and steps the refill bar.

### Health Shield (KQ-319) — `health-shield`
The chip ghost shows what it cost.

A damage model built for legibility: shield absorbs first and shatters when it breaks, then health takes the rest — leaving a chip ghost at the old value that drains a beat later, so you can see exactly what the hit cost. Low health warms the fill and adds a pulse; healing refuses to overfill with a visible bounce at the cap.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/health-shield`

Props:
- `max / start / shield`: number · number · number (default 100 · 78 · 30) — The two pools and the opening health.
- `hit`: number (default 22) — Damage per strike.

Notes:
- The lingering chip ghost is the single most important tell — without it a hit is just a smaller bar.
- Overhealing is refused visibly; a silent cap teaches nothing.
- Reduced motion snaps the bars and shows the ghost as a static beat.

### Mana Orb (KQ-320) — `mana-orb`
Two waves, never in step.

A glass orb of liquid mana whose surface actually moves: two wave layers at different periods, deliberately desynced, because a single sine reads as a machine and two read as liquid. Casting drops the level and sloshes it, an empty cast is refused as clearly as a successful one lands, and regen shimmers until full and then stops.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/mana-orb`

Props:
- `max / start / cost`: number · number · number (default 100 · 62 · 25) — The pool, its opening level, and the spell cost.
- `regenPerSecond`: number (default 3) — Refill rate, driven by a tick counter.

Notes:
- The desynced wave layers are the whole illusion — matching their periods kills it.
- A full orb stops animating; an idle resource should not burn frames.
- Reduced motion flattens the surface entirely and snaps the level.

### Cooldown Dial (KQ-321) — `cooldown-dial`
Four timers, one polyrhythm.

Four abilities with four different cooldowns, which is what gives an ability bar its polyrhythm: each casts, dims, and unwinds its own radial sweep back to ready, with a brief shared lockout after any cast so mashing gains nothing. The return to ready gets its own pop, because the wait is only worth it if the reward is felt.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/cooldown-dial`

Props:
- `abilities`: Ability[] — Name, hotkey, and cooldown seconds per slot.
- `onCast`: (id: string) => void — Fires per successful cast.

Notes:
- Q, W, E, and R cast from the keyboard when the group has focus.
- Remaining time comes from an interval tick counter, never the wall clock.
- Reduced motion shows a stepped numeral instead of an unwinding sweep.

### Boss Meter (KQ-322) — `boss-meter`
The pause is what makes it a phase.

A long fight made legible by its thresholds: the bar carries phase markers, and crossing one stops everything for a beat, stamps the numeral, warms the tint, and names what just changed. That pause is the device — without it a boss bar is just a slow health bar. The last phase enrages, and defeat shatters it.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/boss-meter`

Props:
- `max / hit`: number · number (default 1000 · 85) — The pool and the damage per strike.
- `phases`: number[] (default [75, 50, 25]) — Threshold percentages that trigger a transition.

Notes:
- The phase pause is deliberate dead time — it is what turns a threshold into an event.
- Chip damage lingers here too, at boss scale, so a long fight still reads hit by hit.
- Reduced motion keeps the tint step and stamp but drops the shudder, sweeps, and shatter.

### Sticker Album (KQ-323) — `sticker-album`
The gaps are the ask.

An album page whose empty slots do the asking: each collect flies a sticker to its place, presses it down at a slightly crooked angle, and solidifies the outline. Every fourth pull is a duplicate that slides off to the spares tray — a set you complete without ever pulling a double is not a collection, it is a checklist.

- Duplicates are deliberate: the spares tray is what makes the set feel collected rather than ticked off.

### Badge Case (KQ-324) — `badge-case`
Locked, but never unreadable.

A case of achievements where the locked ones still say what they are: a silhouette, a lock, and the hint that would earn it — because a hidden name teaches nothing about what to chase. - Reduced motion swaps badge states instantly and keeps the caption.

### Passport Stamps (KQ-325) — `passport-stamps`
A perfectly aligned stamp looks printed.

A passport leaf that takes a stamp per destination: the head descends, the page shudders, the mark presses in a degree or two off true, and ink spreads at the edges. A filled page turns to a fresh one. Dates are pre-formatted strings and nothing reads a clock, so the page renders identically everywhere.

### Set Complete (KQ-326) — `set-complete`
The fifth card changes everything.

Five cards and a bonus that stays locked until the last one lands. Pulling a card back re-locks it just as clearly — the loss has to read or the set means nothing.

### Pet Companion (KQ-327) — `pet-companion`
It notices when you stop.

A companion that grows through four stages as your bond rises — and droops, curls up, and dims when it falls, because a pet that cannot be neglected is a toy rather than a companion. Feeding and playing restore it visibly, it blinks on its own, and the mood line always says plainly where you stand.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/pet-companion`

### Journey Map (KQ-328) — `journey-map`
The road lights up behind you.

A winding campaign path where the road lights up behind you: the avatar travels an authored waypoint route while a dash-clipped overlay follows it exactly, so progress reads as ground covered rather than a bar filling. ### Season Track (KQ-329) — `season-track`
The window closes. That is the point.

A two-lane season pass with a closing window: free and premium rows across eight tiers, an unclaimed counter that nags, and a retroactive payout when premium unlocks — which is exactly why the pattern works, shown honestly. Ending the season expires everything unclaimed, in view, because the expiry is the whole point of a season.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/season-track`

Props:
- `tiers / perClick`: number · number (default 8 · 40) — Track length and progress per earn, at 100 per tier.
- `daysLeft`: number (default 12) — Shown in the header; a prop, never computed from a clock.

Notes:
- Unlocking premium pays out every passed tier at once — the retroactive drop is the mechanic, not a bug.
- Expiry greys and strikes unclaimed rewards rather than quietly removing them.
- The track scrolls inside its own container; the page never scrolls sideways.

### Territory Grid (KQ-330) — `territory-grid`
You can only grow from what you hold.

A board two sides expand across, where you may only claim tiles touching what you already hold — so the frontier, not the whole grid, is the decision. Claims ripple into their neighbours, surrounding an enemy tile captures it, and the opponent answers from a fixed sequence so the same board plays the same way for everyone.

- Adjacency gating is the strategy — non-bordering neutrals are inert and look it.
- The opponent replays a fixed sequence; a demo whose rival improvises cannot be reasoned about.
- Reduced motion swaps tile colours instantly and keeps captures and captions.

### Ladder Climb (KQ-331) — `ladder-climb`
Falling is faster than climbing.

A competitive ladder you can fall down, which is the only reason climbing it matters: promotions light the band and unfurl a banner, demotions dim it and say so plainly with no sparks and no ceremony. A demotion shield absorbs the first loss at the bottom of a division, so the fall reads as fair rather than arbitrary.

Notes:

- The shield absorbs one loss at a division floor and regenerates after two wins.
- Reduced motion jumps the marker and keeps both captions.

### Checkpoint Run (KQ-332) — `checkpoint-run`
Progress you cannot lose is a countdown.

A run measured in ground covered, with flags that plant as you pass them and a stumble that throws you back to the last one — quickly, and a little ugly, because losing ground should not look graceful. Progress that cannot be lost is not progress, it is a countdown; the best distance persists so you always have your own mark to beat.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/checkpoint-run`

Notes:
- The stumble is faster than the crawl forward — asymmetry is what makes checkpoints valuable.
- The best distance survives resets; chasing your own mark is the loop.
- Reduced motion snaps the runner back with the caption and no tumble.

### Crit Hit (KQ-333) — `crit-hit`
A crush should not look like a graze.

Damage numbers that scale their weight with what they mean: a graze drifts, a hit rises, a crit punches in with a starburst and a shake, and a crush brings the whole card with it. Numbers fan out along a cycled vector table so a flurry stays readable instead of stacking into a smear. The tier order is fixed, so the same strikes always read the same.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/crit-hit`

Props:
- `tiers`: DamageTier[] — Label, amount, and weight per tier; cycled in fixed order.
- `onCrit`: (amount: number) => void — Fires on the heavier tiers.

Notes:
- Outcomes cycle a fixed table — random crits make a component impossible to reason about or test.
- The fan-out vector table is what keeps a fast flurry legible.
- Reduced motion keeps tier differences in size, weight, and tint, and drops every arc and shake.

### Streak Heat (KQ-334) — `streak-heat`
Cooling is slower than heating.

Escalation you can feel: each multiplier tier warms the panel, grows the numeral, and adds one more ambient layer on top of the last — a pulse, then a shimmer, then a rotating glow, then heat haze. Breaking the streak cools everything down over a slower tween than it took to heat, because a loss should take its time.

Notes:
- The ambient layers are cumulative, not swapped — that stacking is what reads as heat rather than a state change.
- Colour, size, and weight carry the escalation on their own, which is why the reduced-motion fallback still works.
- Reduced motion drops every ambient layer and keeps the ladder legible.

### Perfect Stamp (KQ-335) — `perfect-stamp`

The verdict, slammed onto the results card: it arrives fast and oversized, lands hard at a slight angle, throws a shockwave and dust, and shudders the card by an amount scaled to the grade. ### Impact Frame (KQ-336) — `impact-frame`
The freeze is the feeling.

Hit-stop, demonstrated and measured: an impact freezes the scene for a set number of milliseconds, flashes, jolts within its own bounds, and prints the freeze duration so the effect can be studied rather than just felt. A compare toggle runs the same strike without the freeze, which is the fastest way to understand why it matters.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/impact-frame`

- Reduced motion removes the freeze, flash, jolt, and lines entirely; there is no reduced-but-still-flashing middle ground.
- The printed freeze duration makes this a teaching component as much as an effect.

### XP Shower (KQ-337) — `xp-shower`
The total climbs as they land.

Reward that arrives as objects: orbs burst from the source, hang for a beat, then stream to the counter on staggered arcs — and the total climbs in steps as each one lands, which is the entire reason to do this instead of animating a number. The big orbs are saved for last, because pacing is most of the payoff.

- The hold before the flight is what makes the collection feel deliberate rather than instant.

### Avatar Forge (KQ-338) — `avatar-forge`
Only the changed layer moves.

A character maker where only the layer you changed moves — cycle a head, and the head pops while everything else holds, so the eye lands on the edit instead of hunting for it. A handle is derived from the current combination and rewrites itself as parts change, which is the small thing that turns a shape stack into someone. Saving stamps it into a roster of the last three busts.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/avatar-forge`

- The handle is hashed from the slot indices, so the same avatar always carries the same name.
- Reduced motion swaps parts instantly and keeps the handle, the roster, and the caption.

Heraldry, assembled in order: the shield drops and settles, the field wipes across it, the charge stamps on with a ring, and the ribbon unfurls from the centre carrying the name. ### Unlock Gate (KQ-343) — `unlock-gate`

### Tier Upgrade (KQ-345) — `tier-upgrade`

Status made physical: a membership card that flips into its next self, where the new face only ever comes around mid-flip and is never visible early. ### Mission Board (KQ-346) — `mission-board`

A board you take work FROM, which is a different instrument from a list of what you already hold: postings are pinned and unclaimed, the slots that hold them are few, and accepting one lifts it off its pin and carries it into a slot, leaving the hole behind so the board reads as depleted. ### Return Gift (KQ-347) — `return-gift`

### Focus Rail (KQ-348) — `focus-rail`
One panel is always open.

The primitive behind expanding galleries and team panels: a row of panels where the one under the pointer, or holding focus, grows on a spring while its siblings contract in place. Leaving the rail always restores an expanded panel, because a rail with nothing open reads as broken. Hover expands by default; a press mode waits for a click or Enter, and the keyboard roves either way.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/focus-rail`

Props:
- `items`: FocusRailItem[] — Panels in order; each carries an id, a label, and optional detail content.
- `activeId`: string — Controlled active panel; omit to let the rail manage it.
- `grow`: number (default 2.4) — Flex weight of the expanded panel.
- `expandOn`: "hover" | "press" (default "hover") — Whether hovering expands, or only a press.

Notes:
- Galleries and team sections compose this rather than re-deriving the flex spring.
- Focus always expands the focused panel regardless of mode — keyboard intent is intent.
- Reduced motion resizes panels instantly and swaps detail without fades.

### Turn Modal (KQ-349) — `turn-modal`
Two faces of one object.

A card that lifts, travels to the centre, and turns over on Y into a focus-trapped dialog — the flip and the travel are one motion, so the dialog face comes around mid-flight and is never visible early. Closing reverses the same path back to the card. Where morph-dialog reshapes the trigger into the dialog, this one turns it over, which is the right device when the card and the dialog are two faces of the same object.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/turn-modal`

Props:
- `front`: React.ReactNode — The card face at rest.
- `title`: string — Accessible name of the dialog face.
- `open`: boolean — Controlled open state; pair with onOpenChange.

Notes:
- Focus moves into the dialog once the flight lands and returns to the card on close.
- Both faces hide their backface, so the dialog cannot be read before the turn passes ninety degrees.
- Reduced motion drops the flight and the turn; the dialog fades in centred with the trap intact.

### Elastic Type (KQ-350) — `elastic-type`
Every letter its own spring.

Display text whose glyphs compress under the cursor and rebound when it leaves — each letter its own spring, so a word behaves like a row of rubber blocks. The rebound overshoot on the way back is the signature; without it the effect reads as a squash, not an elastic. Built for 404 numerals and one-word headlines.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/elastic-type`

Props:
- `text`: string — The word or numeral to render.
- `radius`: number (default 120) — Pixel radius of the cursor's influence.
- `squash`: number (default 0.55) — Maximum horizontal compression at the cursor.

Notes:
- The text stays one accessible string; glyph spans are hidden from assistive tech.
- Squash conserves volume — a letter gets taller as it gets narrower — which is what makes it read as material.
- Reduced motion renders the text plainly with no deformation.

### Echo Type (KQ-351) — `echo-type`
Closes like a deck.

Display text with echo layers stacked behind it that fan apart on hover and re-stack when the pointer leaves — fanning staggers outward from the lead, and closing reverses the stagger so the layers fold back like a deck. An always-on mode holds the fan open and breathes it. Built for 404 numerals and single-word headlines that need presence without a backdrop.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/echo-type`

Props:
- `text`: string — The word or numeral to render.
- `echoes`: number (default 5) — Echo layers behind the lead.
- `mode`: "hover" | "always" (default "hover") — Fan on hover and focus, or hold the fan open and breathe it.

Notes:
- Echoes inherit the text colour at falling opacity; nothing animates colour.
- The wrapper is focusable, so a keyboard user fans it too.
- Reduced motion renders the echoes at their fanned positions and holds still.

### Band Type (KQ-352) — `band-type`
Slipping, not leaning.

Display text sliced into horizontal bands that slip sideways under the cursor — the bands nearest the pointer travel furthest, and they alternate direction, which is what makes the word read as slipping rather than leaning. Leave, and the bands settle back top-down on a spring. Built for 404 numerals and one-word headlines.

Install: `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @kinetiq/band-type`

Props:
- `text`: string — The word or numeral to render.
- `bands`: number (default 7) — Horizontal slices.
- `slip`: number (default 28) — Maximum sideways travel in pixels at the cursor.

Notes:
- Bands are clipped copies of one word sized by a hidden reference, so they tile with no seams.
- Touch behaves as a hover at the press point and settles on release.
- Reduced motion renders the word whole and never slices it.
